To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C-terminal helical fragment of Escherichia TRX interacts with the N-terminal portion of the protein and that this interaction is crucial for the folding of TRX.

the C-terminal fragment of thioredoxin interacts with the N-terminal domain to restore the native fold, and that the binding is characterized by an entropic penalty that is compensated by the formation of new hydrogen bonds.

peptide TRX94–108, which includes the last stretch of the C-terminal α-helix (helices 4–5) of E. coli TRX, interacts with TRX1–93, a truncated TRX variant lacking the last stretch of amino acid residues that comprises helix 5, thus restoring the overall TRX structure and catalytic function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a molecular event of peptide recognition that may be relevant in the folding process of TRX and, possibly, other proteins.
the study of a protein folding process where a peptide fragment is recognized and stabilized by a preexisting protein scaffold.

the elucidation of the molecular basis of the TRX folding mechanism, which may have implications for protein folding in general and for the understanding of the folding and assembly processes of multi-domain proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C-terminal helical segment of TRX plays an important role in the folding mechanism of the protein, as well as in its catalytic activity, but is not a structural determinant of the overall fold.
the interaction of the C-helix with the remainder of the molecule is a critical event in the folding mechanism of the TRX fold.
the interaction between the C-terminal helical segment and the remainder of the molecule is a critical event for the folding of TRX.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
peptide recognition is a general phenomenon that may be used for the stabilization of a variety of protein structures.
the C-terminal helices of TRX and TRX1-92 are recognized by peptide TRX94...

the C-terminal helical fragment of TRX is an autonomous folding unit that is able to recognize the remainder of the molecule and to promote folding of the latter, thus leading to a cooperative folding process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interaction of the C-helix with the rest of TRX may represent an important checkpoint in the folding of TRX, a process where the C-terminal helical segment plays a key role.
the C-terminal region of TRX may be involved in the late stages of the TRX folding mechanism.
peptide recognition can be a driving force in the stabilization of a protein fold.
